items.stem: A robot is rewarded for 'distance from the start'. It learns to spin in place at the edge of a cliff to maximise instantaneous distance, risking a fall. What does this illustrate?

options.text: Reward hacking - optimising the stated reward in a way that violates the designer's intent
options.rationale: Correct: the agent exploits a poorly specified reward rather than achieving the intended goal.
The algorithm ran fine; the reward specification was the problem.

options.text: The robot needs a faster processor
options.rationale: Compute is not the issue; the reward design is.
It optimised the reward too literally; that is the point.

items.explanation: Correct: the agent exploits a poorly specified reward rather than achieving the intended goal.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the sim-to-real gap are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Policies trained only in simulation can fail on hardware due to unmodelled dynamics
options.rationale: Correct: differences between sim and reality cause transfer failures.

options.text: Domain randomisation during training can make policies more robust to real variation
options.rationale: Correct: randomising sim parameters helps policies generalise to reality.

options.text: Simulation always matches reality exactly, so transfer is guaranteed
options.rationale: Simulation never matches reality perfectly; that is the gap.

options.text: Real-robot training is always cheaper and safer than simulation
options.rationale: Real-robot training is often costlier and riskier, which is why sim is used first.

items.explanation: Correct: differences between sim and reality cause transfer failures.

items.stem: Why is the exploration-exploitation trade-off central to reinforcement learning?

options.text: The agent must try new actions to discover better returns while still using what it already knows works
options.rationale: Correct: too little exploration misses better policies; too much wastes performance.

options.text: Because exploration and exploitation are the same thing
options.rationale: They are opposing pressures that must be balanced.

options.text: Because the agent never needs to try new actions
options.rationale: Without exploration the agent cannot improve beyond current knowledge.

options.text: Because rewards are irrelevant to action choice
options.rationale: Rewards drive action choice; they are central, not irrelevant.

items.explanation: Correct: too little exploration misses better policies; too much wastes performance.
